title: HALO Trust pilots AWS-supported AI to find explosive remnants in drone imagery of Ukrainian minefields; it may be about 70% accurate, with no clearance outcome yet
summary: HALO announced a US$4m AWS package (25 June 2024) to trial AI on drone imagery of Ukrainian minefields; Reuters (30 April 2026) reports about 70% accuracy; no cleared land or found mine attributed.
account: The HALO Trust announced on 25 June 2024 (page read through the Internet Archive's 20 May 2026 capture) a US$4 million package of support from Amazon Web Services that 'will enable HALO to trial artificial intelligence (AI) to assist in the process of detecting debris of war (including landmines and other explosives) in drone imagery for existing minefields and battlefields in Ukraine', alongside machine-learning detection of damaged buildings in satellite imagery using SageMaker. By then HALO had flown 542 drone flights over Ukrainian minefields, producing 11 terabytes of imagery, and said training would require manually labeling thousands of images and ongoing vetting by HALO staff to remove false positives and negatives. A HALO page of 21 February 2025 describes the pilot through its head of research and development, Matthew Abercrombie, who says an analyst 'can take three to five days to look through the imagery for an average minefield'; it reports no results. Reuters (Sergiy Karazy, 30 April 2026, syndicated by KELO) reported from Myrotske, 40 km north-west of Kyiv, that HALO 'has turned to AI to analyze high-resolution drone imagery of contaminated areas and train systems to identify mines and explosive remnants, achieving around 70% accuracy already', quoting HALO media manager Olena Shustova; the article does not mention AWS and attributes no cleared land, found mine or time saving to the model. The announcement date is used as the date observed because no later milestone is dated.
purpose: Built to flag landmines and other debris of war in drone imagery so that HALO analysts spend less time searching thousands of images per minefield; the pilot is that intended use.
system: HALO Trust AI and machine-learning analysis of drone imagery for explosive remnants of war (hosted on AWS; SageMaker used for satellite-imagery damage detection)
developer: The HALO Trust research and development team with Amazon Web Services
segment: Survey and prioritization of contaminated land by a demining NGO
taxonomy_note: The only figure is a pilot accuracy; faster analyst work is HALO's stated aim, not a result.

ratings.reason: HALO's pages state the aim (three to five analyst-days per minefield) and Reuters gives 'around 70% accuracy'; no time saving, detection count or land release attributable to the model is documented.
No source on file links the AI pilot to any cleared hectare, found mine or avoided casualty in Ukraine.

ai_role.statement: The model is being trained to detect explosive remnants in drone imagery with HALO analysts labeling and vetting outputs; the only performance figure, around 70% accuracy, is reported by Reuters without its basis. The organization's own June 2024 and February 2025 pages report plans and workflow, not results. No independent evaluation, cleared area or detected-mine count is documented.
